BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.contribution: Econometric estimation, causal inference and an applied empirical paper.
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

options.label: Sociology, inequality and social research
options.concept: Sociological theory, qualitative enquiry and quantitative methods anchor this programme. Political science, public economics, history and psychology add perspectives on inequality and social change. Community work and negotiation contribute applied skills, with less specialist inequality, co-creative research and partner-facing intervention training than VU.

options.label: Sociology with digital methods and media analysis
options.concept: Sociological theory and social research are paired with data analysis, machine learning, media studies and AI ethics. The programme examines how media and automated decisions shape social life. UCR develops relevant analytical tools and studies algorithmic fairness, while VU provides dedicated network analysis and a sequence of partner projects.

analysis: Both options retain a substantive sociology core in social theory, identity, collective action and empirical research. The broad programme applies sociology to welfare, education, inequality, institutional change and community engagement. The digital programme combines sociological theory with text and web data, machine learning, media power and an explicit AI ethics course. Its technical work and ethical analysis do not reproduce social-network methods or the structured client projects. Econometrics contributes to causal evaluation through explicit estimation and study of identification but does not reproduce VU’s intervention design. Participatory content in Qualitative Research Methodology contributes to interpretation but does not supply a full co-creative action research module. The project-intensive candidate was reconsidered and would still shift the balance away from sociology into generic business and leadership
